newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-SPARTAK MOSCOW SURGE TO TOP OF TABLE AFTER 4-3 WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPARTAK MOSCOW SURGE TO TOP OF TABLE AFTER 4-3 WIN.

text.p: Spartak Moscow surged to top place in the Russian league on Sunday with just two games remaining after recovering from 1-3 down to win 4-3 at local rivals Torpedo Moscow.
Spartak now have 68 points, one ahead of main rivals Rotor Volgograd who stumbled to a disappointing 0-0 draw away to strugglers Chernomorets Novorossiisk on Saturday.
Defending champions Alania Vladikavkaz ensured they stayed in the hunt by beating bottom side Lada Togliatti 3-0 on Sunday to go third with 66 points.

Spartak, who lost 3-0 at Hamburg in a UEFA Cup tie on Wednesday, started sluggishly and Torpedo's Vyacheslav Kamoltsev appeared to have ensured victory in the 29th minute when his second goal of the game put his side 3-1 up.

But Dmitry Alenichev pulled a goal back with a low shot from just inside the box in the 64th minute and Andrei Tikhonov equalised from the spot in the 77th minute, although the penalty award looked dubious.
Striker Vyacheslav Dzhubanov, a second-half substitute, scored the winner with 10 minutes to go when he scrambled in a diagonal pass from Alenichev at the far post with the Torpedo keeper stranded.
Spartak have lost many of the outstanding players who helped them to the three consecutive Russian championships from 1992-1994 and are by no means guaranteed the title yet.
Next week they are at home to mid-table Rostselmash Rostov while Alania travel to struggling Tekstilshchik Kamyshin, almost certain to be relegated.
Rotor seem to have the toughest match, an away tie at sixth place Lokomotiv Moscow.
Rotor have looked increasingly nervous lately and their 0-0 draw with Chernomorets -- 14th in the 18-team premier division and just two points clear of the relegation zone -- was no surprise.
Rotor's Gennady Yesipov did head the ball into the net in the 19th minute after Oleg Veretennikov's shot had hit the bar, but the referee mysteriously disallowed the effort.
CSKA Moscow, who started Saturday in third place on 63 points, virtually ruled themselves out of the title race by losing 2-1 away to mid-table side Baltika Kaliningrad.
Dynamo Moscow's faint hopes of sneaking the title also ended, thanks to a 3-2 away defeat to struggling 15th placed KamAZ Naberezhniye Chelny.
